title: Architecture & Standards — API, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (Unified Guidelines + ADRs)
author: Priya Desai
body:
Summary and purpose

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It includes normative guidance, operational requirements, and a shortlist of recent Architecture Decision Records (ADRs). The goal is to provide a single reference for engineers and product teams to align on design constraints, SLOs, rollout procedures, and ownership.

Scope
- API standards (REST/HTTP/streaming, error model, versioning, SDK compatibility)
- Coding standards (language-specific conventions, review checklist, linters)
- Infra standards (networking, secrets, infra as code, cloud account boundaries)
- Model-serving standards (model packaging, quantization, KV-cache, batching, fallback variants)
- Observability standards (metrics, traces, logs, dashboards, alerting thresholds)
- Performance standards (latency SLOs, throughput targets, benchmarking suite)

1) API standards

Overview
APIs are the primary contract between Redwood and customer applications. Design for predictable behavior, observable errors, and forward/backward compatibility.

Guidelines
- Use RESTful semantics for resource-style endpoints and streaming endpoints for tokenized generation.
- Stable base path: /v1/{resource}. Versioning strategy: major version in path (e.g., /v1/) for breaking changes; minor/behavioral changes rely on feature flags and documented opt-in parameters.
- Authentication: bearer tokens via Authorization header (Bearer <token>). Short-lived tokens must be supported for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Idempotency: POST endpoints that create resources must accept an optional idempotency-key header.
- Request limits: respond with 429 for rate limits and supply Retry-After header. 429 payload should include quota_scope and estimated_reset.

Error model (JSON)
- Standard error payload: {\"error\": {\"code\": \"<short_code>\", \"message\": \"Human readable message\", \"details\": [\"optional list of strings\"]}}
- Map internal errors to customer-facing classes: unauthorized, forbidden, rate_limited, invalid_request, model_unavailable, internal_error.

Timeouts and retries
- Default client-level timeout: 60s for blocking generation. Streaming endpoints: client should maintain a 120s idle timeout.
- Recommended client retry policy for idempotent calls: exponential backoff with jitter; initial_delay=100ms, max_attempts=4. Do not retry on 4xx except 429.

API example (curl)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-2.1-small\", \"input\":\"Summarize the release notes\"}'

2) Coding standards

General principles
- Follow language-specific idioms and prioritize readability. Default languages: Go (backend infra), Python (ML tooling/evals), TypeScript (console & SDKs).
- Enforce static analysis and formatting via CI (gofmt/go vet; black/ruff; eslint/prettier).
- Minimum review requirements: 1 engineer peer review for trivial changes, 2 reviewers for infra/security/critical runtime changes.

Checklist for PRs
1. Tests added/updated (unit & integration where applicable)
2. Benchmarks updated if performance-sensitive
3. Security review if new secrets/permissions are introduced
4. Docs/CHANGELOG updated (API changes require example)
5. Rollout plan or feature flag included for behavior changes

Secure coding
- Use prepared statements/parameterized queries for any SQL.
- Validate and sanitize all inbound API fields.
- Principle of least privilege for IAM roles.

3) Infra standards

Account and network topology
- Separate cloud accounts: control plane, hosted inference, dedicated customer pools, CI/CD.
- VPCs: use private subnets for GPU hosts; public subnets for load balancers only.

IaC
- Terraform for core infra, organize by service and environment (modules/@namespace). Changes to provider or module versions require signals in PR template and staged rollout.

Secrets and keys
- All secrets must be stored in KMS-backed secret store (AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault for Private).
- Service-to-service auth should use short-lived certificates where supported.

Cost and tagging
- All resources must include tags: team, service, environment, cost_center. Monthly cost review owned by Platform SRE.

4) Model-serving standards

Model packaging and artifacts
- Models must be delivered as a deterministic bundle: model-weights.tar.gz + model-metadata.json + signature/checksum. Metadata fields: model_name, architecture, tokenizer, supported_sequence_lengths, quantization_profiles (if available), compatible_runtimes.

Deployment requirements
- Canary rollout for model version changes: 1) internal smoke tests, 2) 5% traffic canary for 24 hours, 3) increase to 25% for 48 hours, 4) full rollout. Abort thresholds defined below.

Quantization and variants
- Maintain two primary runtime variants per model: full-precision (fp16/f32) and quantized (int8/4bit) where quality regression is validated. Quantization profiles must include expected accuracy delta vs baseline on the official eval suite.

Caching and batching
- Prefix KV cache is enabled by default for conversational endpoints. Cache hit rate target > 25% for stable prompt sets.
- Batching: dynamic batching enabled on GPUs; target batch sizes based on model and latency SLOs (see performance table). Batching should be workload-aware — do not increase queueing delay beyond latency budget.

Fallbacks
- Model fallback policy: if primary model exceeds 95% CPU/GPU utilization or has > 0.5% 5xx error rate for 5 minutes, automatically route to a compatible lower-cost variant in the same region. Ensure functional equivalence and annotate in traces.

5) Observability standards

Metrics (prometheus naming)
- Core metrics (per service/model/route):
  - redwood_request_total{route,model,status} (counter)
  - redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket{route,model} (histogram)
  - redwood_tokens_generated_total{model,customer} (counter)
  - redwood_batch_size_distribution{model} (histogram)
  - redwood_cache_hit_ratio{model} (gauge)
  - redwood_gpu_utilization_percent{instance_type} (gauge)

Tracing
- Use OpenTelemetry for distributed traces. All external API requests must propagate traceparent and include span attributes: service.route, model.version, customer.id (sanitized).

Logging
- Structured JSON logs. Do not log PII or full request payloads. Sampling for high-volume debug logs (default 10%).

Dashboards and SLOs
- Per-model dashboard: request rate, p50/p90/p95/p99 generation latency, error rate, cache hit ratio, tokens/sec.
- SLO examples:
  - Availability: 99.9% successful responses (2xx/3xx) over 30d for hosted API.
  - Latency: p95 generation latency < 500ms for short responses (<=128 tokens) on hosted tier. p99 < 2s.
  - Error budget: 0.1% error budget monthly (aligned to availability SLO).

Alerting thresholds (examples)
- SEV3: redwood_request_error_rate > 0.5% (5m)
- SEV2: p95 latency increase > 2x baseline (10m)
- SEV1: sustained regional GPU pool capacity < 10% available (5m)

6) Performance standards and benchmarking

Benchmark suite
- Use bench-runner (internal) to measure latency/throughput for representative payloads. Benchmarks must be recorded in the benchmarking-and-perf-suite repo and include: model name/version, sequence lengths, batch sizes, runtime kernel, hardware (GPU type), and observed p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies.

Baseline targets (hosted API)
- Small models (<=7B): p95 < 300ms for 64-token responses; throughput target: 2000 requests/s per 8xA100 pool.
- Medium models (7B-30B): p95 < 700ms for 64-token responses.
- Large models (>30B): p95 < 1.5s for 64-token responses; ensure autoscaling policies can handle 2x baseline traffic spikes.

Performance tuning checklist
1. Validate batching configuration (max batch latency and max batch size).
2. Evaluate quantization profiles if latency is above budget.
3. Review kernel selection and CUDA/cuDNN versions.
4. Tune caching (prefix/KV) to improve hit ratio.
5. Re-run benchmark harness and update dashboard baselines.

7) ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) — recent decisions

Table: ADR summary
| ADR ID | Date | Owner | Decision | Link |
|--------|------|-------|----------|------|
| ADR-2026-01 | 2026-01-12 | Liam Chen | Adopt OpenTelemetry + OTLP as our tracing standard | /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-2026-01-opentelemetry |
| ADR-2026-03 | 2026-03-02 | Priya Desai | Standardize model package manifest schema v1.2 | /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/adr-2026-03-model-manifest |
| ADR-2025-11 | 2025-11-20 | Diego Alvarez | Introduce quantized runtime variant as an opt-in for Dedicated tiers | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/adr-2025-11-quant-runtime |

Process for proposing ADRs
1. Create lightweight ADR draft in the ADRs directory using the template (Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives).
2. Circulate for 1 week of review to architecture-standards@redwood (or reviewers listed in PR).
3. If no major objections, mark as accepted and add to change log and related pages.

8) Runbooks and rollouts (critical workflows)

Model rollout abort thresholds (example)
- Abort if 5xx rate > 0.5% above baseline for 30m.
- Abort if end-to-end latency p95 increases > 50% for 30m.
- Abort on any customer-facing data integrity regression (failed outputs per eval suite).

Incident runbook (model-serving latency)
1. Triage: Check per-region dashboard & trace samples. Identify whether issue is CPU/GPU, network, or upstream.
2. Immediate mitigation: Shift traffic away from affected pool (use smart routing) to warm backup pools.
3. If degraded model variant: rollback to previous model version or fallback variant.
4. Post-mortem: capture root cause, timeline, impact, remediation, and follow-up actions.

10) Appendix: config table and examples

Deployment config example (YAML)
---
service: inference-worker
model: redwood-2.1-small
replicas: 8
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_ms: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 64
  cpu_threshold_pct: 70
  gpu_util_threshold_pct: 65
secrets_kms_key: projects/production/kms/redwood-inference
---

Quick CLI: run benchmark
rdw bench run --model redwood-2.1-small --tokens 64 --concurrency 200 --output results/2026-03-10.json

- 2026-01-12: tracing standard adopted (OTel).
- 2026-03-10: harmonized latency SLOs and added performance tuning checklist.
